meta.note: distinct MECHANICS; each can be re-skinned/re-curriculum'd across its also_teaches standards

designs.name: Gadget Repair Shop
designs.mechanic: A broken gadget (toaster, robot, music box) buzzes on the workbench with one glowing empty socket showing an equation like 8 + ? = 13. The child computes the missing addend and drags the matching cog/part with that number into the socket; the gadget whirs back to life.
designs.fun_no_competition: The dead gadget sputters, then lights up and does its silly job (toaster pops bread, robot dances). Gratitude animation: 'You fixed me! Thank you!'
designs.interaction: drag part into socket; tap to test
designs.character_world: Fixit the friendly repair-mole runs a cozy basement repair shop full of personality-rich broken gadgets
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM gadget sprite + CSS socket-glow, drag numbered parts, sprite-swap to 'working' state
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is magic-machine (input→output transformation). Separation: magic-machine produces something NEW from an input; here the gadget is BROKEN and the child must DIAGNOSE the missing value to RESTORE it — the equation is a fault, not a transformation rule, and the payoff is 'fixed/working' not 'created'.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray boxy gadget + empty socket rectangle. CA5: 6-8 gadget characters each in broken (dim, loose part) + repaired (bright, animated) sprite pairs; numbered cog/gear parts

designs.name: Word Doctor's Clinic
designs.mechanic: A 'sick' word lies on the exam cot misspelled (e.g. 'rabbt', 'becuase'). The child taps the wrong/missing letter spot — the X-ray highlights it — then drags the correct letter from the medicine tray to heal it. The word's fever-meter cools to green when spelled right.
designs.fun_no_competition: The word sweats, sniffles, then beams healthy once fixed. Doctor's badge 'All better!' and the patient word hops off the cot saying its name aloud.
designs.interaction: tap to diagnose spot, drag correct letter
designs.character_world: A gentle word-clinic where words are wobbly patients and the child is the caring word-doctor with a stethoscope
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — letter tiles in DOM, highlight class on tapped spot, TTS pronounces the healed word
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is magic-trace (forming letters). Separation: magic-trace is about MOTOR letter formation; here the letters already exist and the skill is DIAGNOSING which letter is wrong/missing and replacing it (orthographic error-detection), not handwriting.
designs.asset_idea: stub: plain letter-tile word on a cot rectangle. CA5: exam-room background, fever-meter, medicine tray of letters, sick→healthy word face overlays

designs.name: Sentence Surgeon
designs.mechanic: An ungrammatical sentence lies on the operating table ('she walk to school', 'the dog are big'). The child taps the faulty word, then drags the corrected form from the tool tray (walk→walks, are→is). A heart-monitor blips healthy when the sentence is grammatically sound.
designs.fun_no_competition: Flatline-to-heartbeat audio when fixed, the sentence sits up on the table smiling and reads itself aloud correctly via TTS.
designs.interaction: tap faulty word, drag corrected form
designs.character_world: A friendly cartoon operating room where sentences are patients with bandages over the broken word
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — tokenized sentence in DOM, tap-to-select token, swap word, TTS read-back
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is story-maker (assembling sentences) and word-doctor (#02 spelling). Separation: story-maker builds from scratch; word-doctor fixes spelling within a single word; this is GRAMMAR/conventions error-correction across a whole sentence (subject-verb agreement, tense), a syntactic diagnosis not an orthographic or compositional one.
designs.asset_idea: stub: sentence tokens on a table line + tray of word chips. CA5: surgeon mole, heart-monitor strip, bandaged sentence patient, tool-tray of replacement words

designs.name: Set the Clock Hands
designs.mechanic: A blank analog clock face with a center pivot. The child grabs the hour hand and the minute hand and drags each around the dial; the hands snap to discrete positions. A prompt names a time ('half past three' / '3:30') and the child draws/rotates the hands to show it, with a digital readout updating live as a scaffold.
designs.fun_no_competition: Spinning the hands feels like turning a real clock; a soft tick as each hand passes a number and a chime when the time is set; no countdown, infinite re-tries.
designs.character_world: Owl's bedtime cottage where setting the right time on the cuckoo clock wakes a cheerful cuckoo.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — atan2 of pointer vs center, snap hour to 12 and minute to step; coupled render (hour advances with minute). Proven in the live E10 clock-core; minimal runtime.
designs.distinctiveness: The produced 'mark' is the drawn hand-angle — a radial-drag generative act, not a tap-the-right-clock choice. Closest neighbor is the existing E10 clock activity (already radial-drag set-the-clock) — this entry is the design-lens articulation of that proven mechanic; separation from magic-trace is that the angle is free-rotated then snapped, encoding the answer, with no dotted guide.
designs.asset_idea: stub: plain circle with numbers + two line hands. CA5 art: carved cuckoo-clock face, owl in nightcap, cozy cottage interior cream/teal.

designs.name: Ten-Frame Tile Restorer
designs.mechanic: A mosaic/wall is broken with chunks missing; the design encodes a teen number as tens-and-ones (a full ten-frame plus loose tiles). The child reads the number ('repair to show 14') and fills the missing tens-block and ones-tiles into the wall to restore the picture, building place-value as restoration.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each tile clicks in restoring the picture; when the number is whole the mosaic shimmers into a finished mural and the mosaic-artist snail beams 'You restored my masterpiece!'
designs.interaction: drag ten-block + ones-tiles into wall gaps
designs.character_world: A snail mosaic-artist whose tile mural cracked and needs a careful tile-restorer's hands
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM ten-frame block + ones cells with empty slots, drag tiles, CSS reveal of underlying mural
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid and Quilt Mender (#03). Separation vs reveal-grid: nothing is hidden-to-uncover; tiles are MISSING and must be supplied per a place-value target. Separation vs #03: #03 fills a single value from a part-whole row; here the child composes tens+ones (1.NBT place value) into a mosaic — a base-ten composition repair, distinct number concept and structure.
designs.asset_idea: stub: ten-frame grid + ones row with empty cells + tile buttons. CA5: cracked mosaic wall, snail artist, ten-block + single-tile sprites, finished mural reveal

designs.name: Number-Line Track Repair
designs.mechanic: A railway/number-line has missing or fallen tick-mark stations between two known numbers. The child drags numbered ties into the gaps so the sequence is correct and evenly spaced, repairing the track so the train can roll across.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each correct tie clicks into place with a satisfying clack; when the gap is whole, a cheery train chugs across the repaired track waving.
designs.character_world: A toy-train valley where a friendly engine is stuck because storm-damaged track needs a track-repair crew
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — horizontal DOM line with gap slots, drag numbered ties, CSS train traversal on completion
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is path-journey (moving along a path). Separation: path-journey is about traversal/progress; here nothing moves until the child RECONSTRUCTS the missing structure of the line itself — placing missing numbers in sequence/skip-count, a number-line completion repair, not a journey.
designs.asset_idea: stub: horizontal line with empty notch slots + numbered tie buttons. CA5: railway ties, wooden train engine character, storm-debris, repaired-track sparkle

designs.name: Torn Picture Mender
designs.mechanic: A photo/storybook page is ripped so part of the SENTENCE caption and image are torn away. The child reads the surviving sentence and chooses the word that correctly completes the meaning (context/comprehension cloze), taping the torn strip back so the picture and caption reunite.
designs.fun_no_competition: The torn strip floats back and tapes shut with a gentle seam-heal; the reunited picture animates (the now-complete scene comes alive) and the caption reads aloud whole.
designs.interaction: drag/tap correct word-strip into the tear
designs.character_world: Granny's photo album / a storybook elf who repairs beloved torn pages so families can remember
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM page with a torn-gap word slot, word-strip choices, CSS seam-mend, TTS read-back
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is Faded Sign (#08) and story-maker. Separation vs #08: #08 restores LETTERS within a known word via phonics; here the missing piece is a whole WORD chosen for meaning/context (comprehension/vocabulary cloze), not decoding. Separation vs story-maker: not free composition — exactly one word fits the existing sentence's sense.
designs.asset_idea: stub: sentence with a blank + word-strip buttons over a picture. CA5: ripped-paper texture, photo-album scene halves, tape seam, storybook elf, reunited animated scene

designs.name: Vet's Diagnosis Window
designs.mechanic: A poorly animal arrives with symptoms shown as a quantity story (e.g. 'ate 12 berries, threw up 5 — how many left in the tummy x-ray?'). The child reads the word-problem, solves it, and dials the correct number into the x-ray machine to diagnose and heal the patient.
designs.fun_no_competition: The right diagnosis dials in, the x-ray glows the answer, and the patient is bandaged, hops up healthy, and nuzzles you with a 'Thank you, doctor!' sticker for the wall.
designs.interaction: read story, dial/tap the result number
designs.character_world: A warm woodland vet clinic where shy animal patients trust the child-vet to figure out what they need
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM story card + number dial/keypad + x-ray panel, sprite swap to healed patient
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is Word Doctor (#02, a clinic) and Recipe Rescue (#06). Separation vs #02: #02 heals SPELLING; this heals via solving a WORD-PROBLEM (math story → take-away/add-to result, 1.OA.A.1) with a diagnosis dial. Separation vs #06: not detecting a wrong quantity but generating the answer to a contextual story to cure a patient.
designs.asset_idea: stub: story text + number keypad + result window. CA5: cozy vet room, sick→healed animal patient pairs, x-ray machine, bandages, gratitude stickers

designs.name: Pattern Rail Builder
designs.mechanic: A train track is missing its next rail-segments. A repeating unit pattern (square-circle-square-circle…, or ABB ABB) is shown; the child snaps the next rail-tiles into the track so the pattern continues correctly. The built track must extend the rule; the engine only rolls forward when the assembled stretch follows the pattern.
designs.fun_no_competition: Rails clack into place with a railway 'cha-clunk'; when the pattern's right the little engine toots and chuffs along the new stretch, dropping a puff of confetti-smoke. Mis-snapped tiles just slide back. Build track forever.
designs.character_world: Chuffer the little blue engine laying its own track across a toy landscape
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — ordered drop-slots; pattern-rule check on the placed sequence; engine slide is a CSS transition
designs.distinctiveness: Not path-journey (traversal) — the child CONSTRUCTS the continuation of the structure and nothing rolls until it's built right. Distinct from sticker-album. This is pattern-extension by assembly: laying segments that obey a unit rule.
designs.asset_idea: stub: rail rectangles with shape icons; CA5 art: wooden toy train rails with shaped tokens, Chuffer engine with chuff-smoke sprite

designs.name: See-Saw Stack
designs.mechanic: A balance beam has two pans. The child stacks unit-blocks onto the left and right pans; the beam tilts in real DOM toward the heavier side. To answer 'make both sides equal' or 'make the left side more', the child adds/removes blocks until the beam settles level or tips the asked direction — the structure's equilibrium encodes the comparison.
designs.fun_no_competition: The wobbly tip-and-settle animation and a delighted 'wheee!' from the two pan-creatures as the beam rocks; landing it perfectly level triggers a sparkle and a held balance pose. No countdown — wobble as long as you like.
designs.character_world: Two round fuzzball friends, Big and Bit, riding a wooden playground see-saw
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — beam rotation via CSS transform tied to a block-count delta; settle = transition, not physics loop
designs.distinctiveness: Not match-pairs (no pairing) and not sort-home. Closest is Tower-of-Tens (01), but there height = a single magnitude; here the BUILT structure on two pans encodes a relation (=, >, <) and the child constructs to a balance condition. Comparison-by-construction.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray beam + square blocks; CA5 art: weathered wooden see-saw, two expressive fuzzball riders, chunky toy blocks

designs.name: Pipe Leak Patch
designs.mechanic: A burst plumbing pipe sprays where a section is missing; the visible flow is labeled with a comparison/equation gap (e.g. left pipe pushes 5, right needs to match — drag the > = < valve or the number that balances). The child patches the correct piece so flow balances and the leak stops. Make the child choose the patch/valve by EVALUATING the comparison (place the < or > or = relation itself), not just picking a pre-correct patch, so it instantiates 1.OA.D.7/K.CC.C.7 rather than decorating it.
designs.fun_no_competition: The right patch snaps in, the spray shrinks to a sealed drip, then the pipe gurgles happily and water flows to fill a fish's tank — the fish thanks you.
designs.interaction: drag patch/valve into the leak gap
designs.character_world: Plumber-otter's underground waterworks; a thirsty fish friend depends on the pipe being fixed
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM pipe segments, spray particle CSS, drag patch, balance check toggles flow animation
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is sort-home and pop-the-right-ones. Separation: those select/route items; here the child evaluates a relational constraint (equality/comparison) to choose the ONE patch that makes a broken system balance — comparison/equality as the diagnostic, with water-physics feedback, not selection or popping.
designs.asset_idea: stub: pipe with a gap + spray + patch buttons. CA5: waterworks tunnel, otter plumber, spray particles, numbered/valve patches, grateful fish in tank

designs.name: The Fair-Trade Post
designs.mechanic: A traveling trader offers a swap: 'I'll give you this drum for 10 acorns.' The child has piles of items and must drag exactly the equal value across the trading log to seal the trade. Trades only 'click' shut when both sides balance; wrong amounts spring back. Each sealed trade adds the new item to your wagon.
designs.fun_no_competition: The satisfying clunk of a balanced trade sealing shut and the trader tipping his hat; your wagon visibly fills with quirky bartered goods you 'own'.
designs.character_world: Pip the badger trader who rolls a wagon between forest stalls, bartering acorns, berries and trinkets.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — two drop-zones, sum-compare on drop, spring-back animation; all DOM + CSS.
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is match-pairs (pairing equal things), but here the two sides are UNLIKE objects of EQUAL VALUE (10 acorns = 1 drum), so the skill is value-equivalence across different units, not visual matching. Distinct from sticker-album because nothing is earned-into-a-slot; you actively give-up value to get value.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray scale-pan + count chips. CA5: badger trader sprite, wagon, acorn/berry/drum item icons, a tipping-hat celebration frame.

designs.name: Tens-Frame Carry Machine
designs.mechanic: A loose-ones bin fills as the child taps to add ones. When it hits 10, the machine AUTO-BUNDLES them into a ten-rod with a satisfying clunk and carries it to the tens column. The child works toward a target number, watching ten ones transform into one ten each time the bin fills.
designs.fun_no_competition: The bin fills, glows, and CLUNKS ten loose ones into a tidy ten-rod that slides over — the auto-bundle transform is deeply satisfying.
designs.character_world: A factory-robot that loves tidying loose blocks into neat bundles
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — DOM unit cubes + CSS bundle-collapse animation + place-value columns
designs.distinctiveness: A transform that fires on a THRESHOLD (ten ones -> one ten) — the cause is reaching capacity, the effect is regrouping. Distinct from combine-split-06 (free merge of two blobs) because this is a place-value bundling triggered automatically at 10. Closest neighbor blob-combine; separation: threshold-bundling vs arbitrary fusion.
designs.asset_idea: stub: unit cubes + bin + ten-rod. CA5: 10-cubes-collapse-to-rod frames, slide-over, robot happy sprites

designs.name: Exact-Change Market Stall
designs.mechanic: A price tag shows the cost (e.g., 47¢). Your coin purse has mixed coins. You drag coins onto the counter to make the EXACT amount — too little and the item won't release, too much and the shopkeeper frowns and hands coins back. On exact change, the item drops into your basket.
designs.fun_no_competition: The 'cha-ching' of an exact-change sale and the item plopping into your basket; you build a basket of treats you bought yourself.
designs.character_world: A cheerful otter shopkeeper at a seaside market stall full of snacks and toys.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — running coin-sum readout, compare to target, release on exact match, return-coins animation on overshoot.
designs.distinctiveness: Pop-the-right-ones is reactive tapping; here it is cumulative VALUE assembly toward a target sum using coin denominations. Distinct from collect-trade-02 (base-ten units) because coins are non-uniform denominations (1/5/10/25), so the skill is money composition to an exact total.
designs.asset_idea: stub: coin chips with values, price card. CA5: otter shopkeeper, penny/nickel/dime/quarter art, basket, market-stall backdrop.

designs.name: Make-the-Total Vending Wall
designs.mechanic: A vending wall shows items each with a small number. You have a target 'pocket money' card (e.g., 'spend exactly 10'). You tap items to add them to your tray; the tray total must hit the target EXACTLY before the slot opens — pick a 6 and a 4, or a 3+3+4. Multiple solutions allowed.
designs.fun_no_competition: Lots of right answers means freedom to pick the snacks YOU want as long as they add up; the slot whirring open feels earned.
designs.character_world: A robot snack-machine named Clunk with a glowing coin slot and rows of cubbies.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — running tray sum, open slot when sum===target, allow many combos.
designs.distinctiveness: Distinct from collect-trade-03 (coin denominations to a money total) — here items carry whole-number 'costs' and the skill is finding addend combinations that sum to a target (decomposition). Not pop-the-right-ones (no single correct item; it's a combination).
designs.asset_idea: stub: numbered tiles + tray total. CA5: robot vending machine, snack icons with cost badges, tray, whirring-open animation.

designs.name: Equivalent-Fraction Swap Meet
designs.mechanic: You hold a fraction tile (e.g., 1/2 of a pizza). A trader offers swaps only when they're EQUAL: trade your 1/2 for 2/4, or 3/6. You drag your tile to a partner tile and the swap seals only if the shaded amounts are identical, growing a collection of 'the same amount, told different ways.'
designs.fun_no_competition: The delight of discovering that two different-looking slices fill the same space; your album fills with 'secret twin' fractions.
designs.character_world: A flamboyant fox trader hosting a tent swap-meet of pies, ribbons and chocolate bars.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — proportional shaded SVG tiles, compare value on swap, seal/reject animation.
designs.distinctiveness: Closest is match-pairs, but match-pairs links identical/paired items; here you swap NON-IDENTICAL representations that are numerically EQUAL (1/2↔2/4). Distinct from collect-trade-01 (whole-unit value) because equivalence is fractional and visual-proportional.
designs.asset_idea: stub: shaded fraction bars. CA5: fox trader, pie/ribbon/chocolate fraction sets, swap-tent backdrop, 'twin' sparkle effect.

designs.name: Word-Family Sticker Vault
designs.mechanic: You earn word-stickers by reading them, but to ADD a sticker to a vault page you must trade it into the page whose RIME it shares (-at page, -ig page). Drag the word 'cat' and it only locks into the -at page; a word that doesn't fit the open pages won't trade in until you flip to its family.
designs.fun_no_competition: Completing a word-family page (all the -at words collected!) and flipping the vault like a real album you filled.
designs.character_world: A squirrel librarian curating a leather word-album in a cozy reading nook.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — word tiles, rime-match gate on drop, album page flip via CSS.
designs.distinctiveness: Sticker-album earns a sticker into a fixed slot; here the trade-in is GATED by phonological rule (the rime must match the page), making it a sort-by-pattern acquisition, and unlike sort-home the items are EARNED-then-traded into a curated collection you flip through.
designs.asset_idea: stub: word cards + labeled pages. CA5: squirrel librarian, ornate album pages per rime, sticker peel/stick animation, reading-nook backdrop.

designs.name: Museum Wing Curator
designs.mechanic: You run a museum wing with a RULE on its banner ('Things that fly', 'Words that start with /b/', 'Shapes with 4 sides'). Exhibits arrive on a conveyor; you accept (drag onto a pedestal) only the ones that meet the rule and wave away the rest. The wing opens to visitors once every pedestal is filled with rule-matching exhibits.
designs.fun_no_competition: The pride of being a curator — your wing fills with a perfect themed collection and ribbon-cutting opens it to little visitor characters.
designs.character_world: A bow-tied penguin museum director with a conveyor of crated exhibits.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — conveyor of items, rule-check on pedestal drop, wave-away animation, ribbon-cut when full.
designs.distinctiveness: I-spy-scene is find-in-a-cluttered-picture; this is accept/reject acquisition against a category RULE to CURATE a set. Distinct from sort-home (multi-bin sorting) — here there's ONE wing and a binary keep/decline gate building a themed collection you own and 'open.'
designs.asset_idea: stub: item cards + pedestals + rule banner. CA5: penguin curator, museum hall, exhibit pedestals, conveyor crates, ribbon-cutting frame.

designs.name: Set-Completer Card Packs
designs.mechanic: You open card packs revealing items, then assemble a COMPLETE SET defined by a counting/numeral rule — e.g., a 'family' set is all five cards numbered 1–5 in order, or a 'rainbow' set is one of each color count. You drag cards into the album's empty numbered frames; the set closes (with a fanfare) only when every frame is correctly filled.
designs.fun_no_competition: Tearing open a pack and the gotta-complete-the-set thrill; the album spread lighting up gold when a set finishes.
designs.character_world: A raccoon collector trading-card shop with foil packs and binder pages.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — pack-open reveal, numbered frame targets, validate full-set completion.
designs.distinctiveness: Sticker-album fills one slot per earned sticker; here completion requires the WHOLE ordered/numbered set to be assembled correctly (1,2,3,4,5 in their frames), making sequence/cardinality the skill. Reveal-grid uncovers hidden cells — here cards are revealed then PLACED by number.
designs.asset_idea: stub: numbered cards + frames. CA5: raccoon shopkeeper, foil card packs, binder pages, foil-shimmer + set-complete fanfare.

designs.name: Synonym Swap Bazaar
designs.mechanic: A trader wants a word but won't take just any — they'll only accept a word that MEANS THE SAME as the one on their sign ('big' wanted → trade in 'huge' or 'large', not 'small'). You browse your word-pouch and drag a synonym across; a fair meaning-trade seals and you collect the trader's prize word into your vocabulary chest.
designs.fun_no_competition: The 'aha' of finding a word that means the same; collecting a chest of trader-prize words that are yours.
designs.character_world: A peddler parrot in a colorful word-bazaar tent, squawking the wanted word.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — synonym-set lookup gates the trade; small curated word lists per round.
designs.distinctiveness: Distinct from match-pairs (pairs identical/linked items) because the trade is gated by MEANING-equivalence (synonyms), not identity. Distinct from word-family vault (-06) which gates by sound/rime; this gates by semantic equivalence — the vocabulary analog of a fair value trade.
designs.asset_idea: stub: word tiles + wanted-sign. CA5: parrot peddler, bazaar tent, word-pouch + treasure chest, seal-the-trade sparkle.

designs.name: Antonym Trading Post
designs.mechanic: The trader posts a word and wants its OPPOSITE in exchange ('hot' → bring 'cold'). You search your word-crates for the antonym and trade it across; a correct opposite seals the deal and earns you the next word for your opposites album. Wrong-meaning trades are politely declined.
designs.fun_no_competition: The playful twist of trading a word for its mirror-image; filling an 'opposites' album with paired-up words.
designs.character_world: A hedgehog trader at a frontier trading post with crates of word-cards.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — antonym-pair lookup gates the trade; curated opposite lists.
designs.distinctiveness: Mirror of synonym swap (-10): the gate is OPPOSITE-meaning rather than same-meaning, a genuinely different semantic relationship (antonyms) and CCSS skill. Both are fair-meaning trades, but the relation flips, which young children find a distinctly different cognitive task.
designs.asset_idea: stub: word cards + wanted-opposite sign. CA5: hedgehog trader, frontier post, word-crates, opposites-album spread, deal-sealed stamp.

designs.name: Same-Time Clock Trader
designs.mechanic: A trader shows a time one way (a clock face at 3:30) and only trades for a card showing the SAME time told differently ('half past three', a digital 3:30, or 'thirty minutes after three'). You hunt your card stash for the matching-meaning time and trade it across to collect the prize.
designs.fun_no_competition: Discovering that an analog face and the words mean the same moment; collecting matched time-pairs into a clockmaker's case.
designs.character_world: A wise tortoise clockmaker trading in a shop of ticking clocks.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — render analog SVG clock + word/digital cards, equality check on time value.
designs.distinctiveness: An equivalence trade in the TIME domain: different representations of the same time are 'equal value.' Distinct from equivalent-fraction swap (-04, proportional area) and synonym swap (-10, meaning) — same structural trade, new content domain, and it directly teaches time-telling equivalence.
designs.asset_idea: stub: clock face + time cards. CA5: tortoise clockmaker, clock-shop backdrop, analog faces, digital + word cards, matched-pair glow.

designs.name: Tally-Token Earn & Spend
designs.mechanic: A scene shows things to count (e.g., 7 frogs). You count and earn that many tally-tokens, which drop into your jar. Then a shop card says 'this lily-pad costs 7 tokens' — you spend the EXACT tokens you earned to buy it. Earn-by-counting, spend-by-exact-amount; the jar must zero out for a clean purchase.
designs.fun_no_competition: Counting fills your jar with a happy plink-plink; spending it all on the thing you wanted feels like a real shopping trip.
designs.character_world: A frog merchant on a lily-pad market selling pond goods for tally-tokens.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — count scene items → token count, spend exact tokens, validate jar empties on purchase.
designs.distinctiveness: Tokens are an explicit earn-then-spend medium tied to counting, not a score. Distinct from make-the-total (-05) which is combination-to-target; here it's a single count-then-match-and-spend loop (cardinality → exact spend). The earn step (count the scene) and spend step (pay exactly) are two linked acts.
designs.asset_idea: stub: countable scene + token jar + shop card. CA5: frog merchant, lily-pad market, tally-tokens, jar fill/empty animation.

designs.name: Rhyme-Coin Gumball Shop
designs.mechanic: Each gumball machine takes a 'rhyme-coin' — a word that rhymes with the machine's label ('cake' machine takes 'lake', 'rake', 'snake'). You earn word-coins by reading them, then feed the RIGHT-rhyming coin into a machine to collect its gumball prize. Non-rhyming coins are spat back out.
designs.fun_no_competition: The clunk-and-roll of a gumball dropping when you feed the right rhyme; collecting a rainbow of gumball prizes per machine.
designs.character_world: A bear shopkeeper's penny-arcade of colorful gumball machines.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — rhyme-set gate per machine, spit-back animation on miss, gumball-drop on match.
designs.distinctiveness: Earn-and-spend where the currency is gated by RHYME (a sound relationship) rather than value or meaning. Distinct from word-family vault (-06, rime-spelling pages) because rhyme here is auditory (read/heard) and the spend act is feeding a machine to collect, not filing into an album.

designs.name: Measure-and-Match Length Trader
designs.mechanic: A trader wants 'a stick exactly 5 units long.' Your stash has objects of various lengths shown against a unit ruler. You measure (count units) and drag across only the object whose length EQUALS the wanted measure, trading it for a collectible. Different objects, same length count as a fair trade.
designs.fun_no_competition: Laying objects against the ruler to find the one that fits; collecting a workshop of just-right-length treasures.
designs.character_world: A beaver builder-trader whose workshop trades parts measured by a unit ruler.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — render objects spanning N ruler units, compare unit-length to wanted, seal on equal.
designs.distinctiveness: An equivalence trade in the LENGTH/measurement domain — value = unit-length. Distinct from same-time trader (-12) and fraction swap (-04) by content, and from i-spy because the gate is a measured-equality (count the units) rather than visual search.
designs.asset_idea: stub: ruler + variable-length bars. CA5: beaver builder, workshop backdrop, ruler, length-objects (ribbons/sticks), trade-seal animation.

designs.name: Bridge the Gap
designs.mechanic: A river gap of N planks-wide separates two cliffs. The child drags numbered plank-segments (lengths 1–10) and lays them end-to-end to span exactly the gap. For addition gaps ('the gap is 7, you have a 3-plank — what plank completes it?') the child must select and place the missing-length plank so the bridge meets the far edge with no overhang or shortfall.
designs.fun_no_competition: When the last plank clicks flush, the bridge plays a wooden 'ka-thunk', tiny lanterns light along it, and a hedgehog hops across happily. Overhang gives a gentle springy bounce-back, never a buzzer. Rebuild freely.
designs.character_world: Pip the hedgehog, a tiny builder crossing forest streams plank by plank
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — planks are width-sized divs snapping to a grid track; fit check = sum of placed widths vs gap width
designs.distinctiveness: Path-journey is about traversing a route; here nothing travels until the bridge is COMPLETE and the structure must measure-fit exactly. Distinct from number-line tools because the planks are physical segments the child assembles; the made-to-measure span encodes the addend/length. Different from Brick-Blueprint (2D fill) — this is 1D linear length composition.

designs.name: Syllable Skyscraper
designs.mechanic: A word's picture sits at the top; the child builds a tower by stacking one 'floor-block' per syllable they hear — clap-and-stack. For 'butterfly' (but-ter-fly) they stack 3 floors; each floor lights as they tap it. The finished tower's height must equal the syllable count, and tapping each floor replays that syllable chunk.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each floor 'pops' into place with a chime as a window lights up; the top floor sprouts a little rooftop flag and a window-cat waves. Clap and rebuild as many words as you like — no timer.
designs.character_world: A city of cozy little buildings where word-cats live one floor per syllable
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — stacked floor divs, audio chunks from existing TTS/clip set; height vs syllable count check
designs.distinctiveness: This is ELA-as-construction: syllable count = building height. Not story-maker (no sequence of events) and not magic-trace. Closest math neighbor is Tower-of-Tens, but here height encodes a phonological count from listening, not a number magnitude — recognition-first, no letter production.
designs.asset_idea: stub: stacked rectangles as floors; CA5 art: whimsical storybook apartment floors with lit windows, rooftop flag, peeking window-cats

designs.name: Word Wall Bricks
designs.mechanic: Onset and rime bricks (sh-, -ip; b-, -at) are mortared into a wall. The child slides a target picture's bricks together — they snap with a satisfying mortar-squish ONLY when the onset and rime combine into a real word naming the picture. Building the wall word-by-word, each correct brick-pair becomes a solid block in the growing wall.
designs.fun_no_competition: The mortar-squish 'splat' and the blended word spoken aloud when bricks fuse; the wall slowly becomes a snug little house you keep. A bricklayer beaver nods approval. No scoring, just a house that grows.
designs.character_world: Barnaby the beaver mason building a cottage wall out of word-bricks
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — two brick halves snap into a slot; validity = lookup against approved-words list; TTS blends on join
designs.distinctiveness: Not match-pairs (which pairs two equals) — here two DIFFERENT segment-types assemble into one new unit (a word), and the wall is a persistent growing structure you construct. Distinct from Syllable-Skyscraper (05, counting/height) — this is segment-assembly into words (blending), not counting.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two-tone rectangles with text; CA5 art: clay bricks with wet mortar texture, a half-built cottage, Barnaby beaver with a trowel

designs.name: Blueprint Tiles
designs.mechanic: A faint blueprint outline shows a target shape made of unit-square tiles (e.g. a 3×4 rectangle). The child lays individual square tiles onto the grid to fill the blueprint exactly. When complete, the structure is partitioned and the child taps to count rows/columns — the assembled array reveals the row-and-column structure.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each tile snaps with a ceramic 'tick'; finishing the floor makes the whole pattern shimmer and a little gecko skitters across the new tiles delightedly. Rows glow as you count them. No timer — re-tile any pattern.
designs.character_world: Tilly the gecko, a mosaic-floor artist decorating sunny courtyards
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — CSS grid drop-zones; fill-check = all blueprint cells covered; row/col tap-count is index math
designs.distinctiveness: Not reveal-grid (which uncovers hidden cells) — here the child PLACES tiles to construct a 2D array from nothing, against a plan. Distinct from Brick-of-Tens; this teaches array/area structure (rows × columns) by physical tiling, the foundation of multiplication and area.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray grid + colored squares; CA5 art: glossy Mediterranean mosaic tiles, a courtyard floor, Tilly the gecko sprite

designs.name: Fraction Pie Bakery
designs.mechanic: An empty pie-tin shows a target like '3/4'. The child drags equal wedge-pieces (the bakery only stocks halves, thirds, fourths…) and fits them into the tin until the assembled pie shows exactly the fraction — they must pick the right-size wedges and place the right COUNT so the built pie matches the label and leaves the correct empty arc.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each wedge slots in with a soft 'plip' and a puff of cinnamon sparkles; a completed pie steams and a chef raccoon rings a tiny bell. Wrong-size wedges gently bounce out — no buzzer. Bake endless pies.
designs.character_world: Rocco the raccoon baker in a warm fraction-pie bakery
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — wedge divs with rotation transforms slotting into a circular tin; fit-check = correct denominator wedges × count
designs.distinctiveness: Not sort-home or match-pairs. This is construction-to-a-fraction: the child assembles a partitioned whole from equal pieces, fitting wedges so the structure equals the target. Distinct from Blueprint-Tiles (07, square array) — radial equal-partition of a whole, teaching unit fractions by building.
designs.asset_idea: stub: pie-circle + colored wedge sectors; CA5 art: golden lattice pie wedges, a cozy bakery tin, Rocco raccoon with a chef hat

designs.name: Sentence Scaffold
designs.mechanic: A sentence is built like scaffolding: word-cards (a capital-start word, naming/action words, an end-mark) must be assembled left-to-right into a frame so the structure reads as a complete, correctly-ordered sentence — capital brick first, period/question brick last. The child stacks word-bricks into the frame; the scaffold only locks when the order forms a valid sentence.
designs.fun_no_competition: Word-bricks clink as they lock into the scaffold; a completed sentence is read aloud and the scaffold lifts to reveal a little illustrated scene of the sentence. A friendly fox foreman gives a thumbs-up. Rebuild freely.
designs.character_world: Sentence-Site, a tiny construction yard run by Felix the fox foreman
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — ordered slot frame; valid-order check (capital first, end-mark last, known sentence templates); TTS reads it
designs.distinctiveness: Not story-maker (which sequences scene/events) — here the child constructs ONE grammatical sentence as a built structure, enforcing capitalization-first and end-punctuation-last via the scaffold shape. Distinct from Word-Wall-Bricks (06, sub-word blending) — this is sentence-level word-order assembly.
designs.asset_idea: stub: word-label rectangles in a frame; CA5 art: scaffolding poles with chunky word-bricks, a hard-hat fox foreman, reveal scene cards

designs.name: Nesting Number Boxes
designs.mechanic: A set of open boxes of graduated sizes must be nested smallest-inside-largest. Each box is labeled with a quantity (a dot-set or numeral); the child fits them so they nest in the correct ORDER of value — a box can only go inside one holding a larger number. Building the full nested stack orders the numbers concretely.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each box drops inside the next with a wooden 'tonk' and a peg-doll pops up waving; closing the final lid plays a music-box twinkle. Wrong fits bob back out gently. Nest and un-nest endlessly.
designs.character_world: A shelf of cheerful Russian-doll-style stacking boxes with peg-doll friends inside
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — size-scaled divs with containment validity = value ordering; no physics, pure logic + transitions
designs.distinctiveness: Not sort-home (binning) — physical fit-nesting where size/containment encodes magnitude order, and a wrong-value box literally won't fit. Distinct from See-Saw-Stack (02, two-way comparison) — this is full ordering/seriation of a whole set by construction.
designs.asset_idea: stub: nested squares with numbers; CA5 art: painted matryoshka-style nesting boxes, peg-doll characters, a sunny shelf backdrop

designs.name: Number Bond Bridge
designs.mechanic: A whole-number block sits atop two empty support-pillars (the parts). The child stacks unit-cubes into the two pillars so the two part-heights TOGETHER hold up the whole (part + part = whole). For 'make 10', if one pillar is built to 6, the child must build the other to 4 or the whole block tilts and won't rest level.
designs.fun_no_competition: When the parts make the whole, the top block settles with a contented 'clunk' and tiny carved faces on the pillars smile; a lopsided build wobbles cutely until fixed. A builder badger gives a wink. Re-decompose endlessly.
designs.character_world: Bramble the badger building little bridges held up by two stone pillars
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — two stack columns + a beam div; level-rest check = pillar1Count + pillar2Count === whole
designs.distinctiveness: Not See-Saw (02, comparison balance across a fulcrum) — here two pillars SUPPORT one whole, encoding part-part-whole decomposition by load-bearing structure. Distinct from Tower-of-Tens (single column magnitude); this is composing/decomposing a number into two addends via twin supports.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two cube columns + a bar; CA5 art: carved stone pillars with friendly faces, a wooden whole-block beam, Bramble badger sprite

designs.name: Gear Train Builder
designs.mechanic: A crank turns a first gear; the child must fit intermediate gears into pegs so the chain connects crank → target wheel. The number of teeth / spacing acts as a skip-count: placing the right gears makes the final wheel turn, and a counter ticks the skip-count (2,4,6…) as teeth mesh. Building a working gear-train that meshes is the skill.
designs.fun_no_competition: When the last gear meshes, the whole train spins with a happy whirr and a string of bells chimes the skip-count; un-meshed gears just sit still. A tinkerer hedgehog claps oil-stained mitts. Tinker as long as you like.
designs.character_world: Gizmo the tinkerer hedgehog in a clockwork workshop
designs.web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — rotating meshed gears that visually drive each other want SVG rotation sync; mesh-validity logic is simple, but smooth coupled rotation is borderline for pure CSS
designs.distinctiveness: Not magic-machine (rule-based transform of input→output) — the child engineers the structural CHAIN; nothing turns until gears physically mesh in the right positions. The build encodes skip-counting / equal-groups. Distinct from Pattern-Rail (09, linear pattern) — this is a 2D connectivity-and-mesh construction.
designs.asset_idea: stub: circle divs as gears on a peg-board; CA5 art: brass cogs with visible teeth, a workbench, Gizmo hedgehog with a wrench

designs.name: Comparison Wall
designs.mechanic: Two side-by-side towers must be built to two given quantities, then the child constructs a comparison-symbol brick (>, <, =) and snaps it into the gap between the towers so the open mouth faces the taller tower. The built towers plus the placed symbol assemble a true comparison statement.
designs.fun_no_competition: The symbol-brick gulps toward the bigger tower with a cartoon 'chomp', the towers do a little victory shimmy, and a crocodile mascot (the > 'hungry mouth') grins. No buzzer — re-snap the symbol freely.
designs.character_world: Chompy the comparison-crocodile who always faces the bigger number
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — two stack columns + a draggable symbol brick; validity = symbol orientation vs tower-height comparison
designs.distinctiveness: Not See-Saw (02, physical balance) and not Nesting-Boxes (12, ordering by fit) — here the child builds two explicit towers to numerals AND assembles the relational symbol, producing a written comparison (12 > 8). Construction yields a symbolic statement, not just a felt relation.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two cube columns + </>/= brick; CA5 art: two block towers, a toothy croc-mouth symbol-brick sprite, sunny block-yard

designs.name: Compound Word Crane
designs.mechanic: A crane lifts whole-word blocks (sun, flower, rain, bow, butter, fly). The child fuses two blocks together by lowering one onto another; they snap and weld into one bigger compound-word block ONLY if the two words make a real compound (sun+flower=sunflower). The crane then sets the new welded block onto the structure being built.
designs.fun_no_competition: The weld throws cute friendly sparks, the new word is spoken aloud, and the crane operator squirrel cheers 'sunflower!'; non-compounds just clink apart unharmed. Build a whole compound-word skyline. No timer.
designs.character_world: Skip the squirrel crane-operator on a word-block construction site
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — two word divs merge into one; validity = lookup in a compound-word list; TTS speaks the result
designs.distinctiveness: Not Word-Wall-Bricks (06, onset+rime sub-word blending) — here two FULL words assemble into a compound word, a morphological build at the word level. Not match-pairs (no equal-pairing). The weld-into-one mechanic encodes compound-word formation.
designs.asset_idea: stub: word rectangles + a crane hook line; CA5 art: a toy crane, chunky welded word-blocks, Skip squirrel in a hard hat

designs.name: Symmetry Builder
designs.mechanic: Half a creature/butterfly is drawn on the left of a mirror-line; the child places tiles/parts on the right side to BUILD the mirror image so the finished structure is symmetric. Each part must be set in the position that reflects its twin across the line — completing the symmetric build reveals the whole creature.
designs.fun_no_competition: Each mirrored part snaps in with a glassy 'ting' and a soft glow ripples across the mirror-line; completing the symmetry makes the butterfly flap its now-whole wings and flutter up. Off-spots gently float back. Build symmetric creatures endlessly.
designs.character_world: Iris the firefly, painting symmetric butterflies in a moonlit garden
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — left art is fixed; right drop-zones validate against reflected coordinates; flutter is a sprite animation
designs.distinctiveness: Not dress-decorate (free aesthetic placement) — every part has ONE reflection-correct spot, so the build enforces line-symmetry. Not Blueprint-Tiles (07, blueprint copy) — here the 'plan' is a mirror constraint the child must compute, not trace. Spatial-reasoning-by-construction.
designs.asset_idea: stub: half-image + mirror line + part dots; CA5 art: glowing butterfly wing halves, a dewy garden, Iris firefly with a glow-trail

designs.name: Slice the Snack
designs.mechanic: A whole food shape (pizza, cookie, cake) sits on a plate. The child drags one finger to draw a straight cut line across it; the line snaps to the nearest valid cut and the shape splits along it. The child draws enough cuts to make the requested number of EQUAL parts (halves, thirds, fourths), and each completed equal slice gently lifts and animates.
designs.fun_no_competition: The satisfying SPLIT — the shape cleanly cleaves and the slices spring apart with a soft pop; no timer, you can cut as many times as you like and wrong cuts just bounce off without splitting.
designs.character_world: A friendly Baker Bear's snack stand where every treat needs fair-sharing cuts for the animal customers.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — SVG shape with a small set of valid cut-axes per shape; the child's drawn stroke is reduced to its endpoints/angle and snapped to the nearest valid axis, then equality is checked combinatorially against the target part-count. Free-draw is constrained to a snap set, avoiding hard free-form evaluation.
designs.distinctiveness: The produced mark IS the partition — the cut line the child draws encodes the fraction, not a tap-the-pre-cut-piece choice. Closest neighbor is the existing E14 fractions recognition (tap the already-equal shape) and magic-trace (follow a fixed dotted guide); separation: here the child GENERATES a free-drawn cut line that is snap-evaluated for equal partition, the active-partition facet explicitly deferred in E14.
designs.asset_idea: stub: plain colored circle/square/rectangle on a gray plate. CA5 art: warm cream-and-coral baked goods (round cookie, square brownie, rectangular cake), Baker Bear, soft plate with crumb texture.

designs.name: Draw the Mirror Line
designs.mechanic: A complete symmetric object (snowman, vase, ladybug, capital letter A) is shown. The child draws a single straight stroke they think is the line of symmetry. On release the figure 'folds' along their drawn line: if it folds onto itself the two halves glow and lock; if not, the figure wobbles back unfolded so they can try a different stroke.
designs.fun_no_competition: The whole figure hinges and folds along your line like real paper — a tactile snap when it lands on itself; figures with multiple symmetry lines accept any correct one and sparkle each found line.
designs.character_world: A folding-paper workshop where each cut-out shape hides one or more secret mirror lines to discover.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — drawn stroke reduced to a line; reflect the figure's vector outline across it and compare overlap with the original (point-sample or path-distance) within tolerance. Pre-known axes per asset make the check a simple angle/offset match.
designs.distinctiveness: Here the child draws the AXIS onto a finished figure and the figure self-tests by folding along the drawn stroke — distinct from 02 (fold a half to build the whole) and from magic-trace (no fixed dotted guide; the child must locate the line themselves). The drawn mark is the answer-line.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray symmetric outlines (vase, heart) on grid. CA5 art: paper-craft snowman, ladybug, vase, butterfly, big block letters; teal cutting-mat backdrop.

designs.name: Cut the Ribbon into Units
designs.mechanic: A long ribbon/tape lies along a ruler. The child drags scissors to draw cut marks across the ribbon at unit intervals to divide it into the requested number of equal pieces (cut a 6-unit ribbon into 6 one-unit pieces, or into 2 threes). The ribbon snaps cuts to whole-unit tick marks and each cut piece falls and stacks.
designs.fun_no_competition: The crisp snip sound and the pieces tumbling into a neat stack; cuts snap to ticks so it always looks tidy; lenient — extra ticks just don't cut.
designs.character_world: A gift-wrap mouse who needs ribbons measured and snipped into fair lengths for the party parcels.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — ribbon is a rectangle over a tick scale; drawn cross-stroke snaps to nearest tick, splits the segment array; check piece-lengths equal/match target. Snap set keeps evaluation trivial.
designs.distinctiveness: Linear partition of a LENGTH by drawn cut-marks against a unit ruler — distinct from 01 (2D area partition of a shape into equal fractions) and from build/sort templates. The cut positions encode iteration of a length-unit (measurement), not area-fraction.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray bar over numbered ruler + scissor icon. CA5 art: glossy coral ribbon, brass scissors, gift-wrap mouse, parcels with bows.

designs.name: Connect the Dots: Count to Reveal
designs.mechanic: Scattered numbered dots hide a picture. The child draws one continuous trail from dot 1 to 2 to 3... in order; the line only 'sticks' to the next correct number in sequence and rejects out-of-order dots. When the last dot connects, the outline closes and the hidden creature fills in with color and animates.
designs.fun_no_competition: The classic dot-to-dot delight — the picture emerging line by line and bursting into color at the final dot; wrong-order dots just don't connect, no penalty, gentle pulse points to the next number.
designs.character_world: A 'star-stitcher' firefly drawing constellations that turn into glowing animals.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — dots are points with an order index; track which dot the pointer is over, append to path only if it equals expected+1. Pure sequence check, no free-form geometry evaluation.
designs.distinctiveness: Generative ordered-trail drawing where the child's free path must visit dots in numeric (or alphabetic) sequence — the trail is the answer. Distinct from path-journey (navigate a fixed maze) because the child CONSTRUCTS the connecting line, and from magic-trace (no pre-drawn dotted outline; the order is the puzzle). Reveal is the payoff.
designs.asset_idea: stub: numbered dots on dark field + plain line. CA5 art: firefly with a glowing thread, dot-constellation that fills into a fox/whale, night-sky teal gradient.

designs.name: Shade the Fraction
designs.mechanic: A shape pre-divided into equal parts (a 4-part chocolate bar, an 8-slice pizza outline) is shown empty. A prompt asks for a fraction (3/4, 5/8). The child drags a finger to PAINT/shade regions; each region fills fully when touched and un-fills if tapped again. They shade exactly the requested number of parts and the bar 'tastes ready' when the count matches.
designs.fun_no_competition: The smooth swipe-to-fill, like coloring perfectly inside lines automatically; a yummy shimmer when the right amount is shaded; over-shade just lifts back off, no fail state.
designs.character_world: A chocolatier fox filling fraction-bars and pizza orders by the painted slice.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — each part is an SVG region with a filled boolean toggled by pointer-over; count filled vs target. No free-form geometry; coloring is region-snapped.
designs.distinctiveness: Region-shading where the painted area encodes the numerator over the pre-set denominator — a free paint-to-fill act, not a tap-one-piece choice and not a partition-cut. Closest neighbor is 01 (the child here does NOT create the partition; they shade an existing equal partition to show a quantity). Distinct from reveal-grid (no hidden picture; the fill IS the math).
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray bar split into N cells. CA5 art: chocolate bar with embossed squares, pizza with slice lines, chocolatier fox, warm brown/cream.

designs.name: Ring the Groups
designs.mechanic: A scattered set of objects (10 acorns) sits in a clearing. The child draws free-form loops/rings around objects to partition the set into equal groups (draw 2 rings of 5, or 5 rings of 2). Each closed loop counts the objects inside it; rings glow green when all rings hold the same equal count.
designs.fun_no_competition: Lassoing objects with a glowing loop and watching the count tally pop above each ring; equal rings sparkle together; uneven rings just stay neutral, redraw freely.
designs.character_world: A squirrel sorting its acorn hoard into fair piles for winter, drawing chalk circles in the dirt.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — point-in-polygon counting of a free-drawn closed loop is doable (ray-casting on the drawn path) but loops must be auto-closed and validated; honest flag: robust free-loop capture + which-objects-inside is moderate. Mitigate by snapping objects to a coarse grid so enclosure is cell-based.
designs.distinctiveness: Free-drawn enclosure loops partition a SET (discrete grouping / early multiplication & division readiness) — the drawn ring is the answer. Distinct from sort-home (drag into bins) because the child draws the boundary themselves, and from 01/05 (continuous shape/length partition; this is discrete-set equal grouping).
designs.asset_idea: stub: dots on a grid + chalk loop. CA5 art: acorns, leaves, a squirrel with a tiny chalk stick, forest-floor texture, teal chalk loops.

designs.name: Draw the Missing Half
designs.mechanic: Half of a symmetric picture is printed; the other half is a faint mirrored grid-guide. The child draws their own strokes to complete the second half, square by square, using the grid to copy. As each grid cell's drawn line lands near the target mirror-path it locks in; finishing reveals the full colored picture.
designs.fun_no_competition: The pride of drawing the matching half yourself and seeing it 'click' true at each square; the picture colors in once symmetric; very forgiving snap, no erasing penalty.
designs.character_world: An art-class panda showing how to finish mirror-pictures square by square.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: needs-richer-runtime — evaluating free strokes against a target path per grid cell requires path-distance tolerance checks; feasible per-cell but more involved than snap-set games. Honest: simplify by checking whether each guide cell has been substantially covered by ink rather than exact stroke shape.
designs.distinctiveness: Generative copy-by-symmetry drawing — the child PRODUCES the mirror half stroke by stroke (lenient grid-snap), reinforcing symmetry through making rather than recognizing. Distinct from 02 (drag a ready-made half) and 03 (draw just the axis line); here they draw the actual missing form. Lenient grid-cell tolerance keeps it K-3-true.
designs.asset_idea: stub: half a gray figure + faint grid on the empty side. CA5 art: half-printed house/tree/face, soft pencil-grid, panda in an art smock, cream paper.

designs.name: Trace to Write the Numeral
designs.mechanic: A 'how many' prompt shows a quantity (4 ducks). The child counts, then traces the corresponding numeral along directional arrows — but the guide is faint and lenient; the stroke just needs to follow the general path top-to-bottom in the right order. Correct count + traced numeral makes the ducks cheer.
designs.fun_no_competition: The reward of forming a real number with your finger and the counted objects celebrating; arrows light up as you pass them; very forgiving, restart the stroke anytime.
designs.character_world: Counting Ducklings pond, where writing their number makes that many ducklings line up and quack.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — numeral as a directional stroke-path with ordered checkpoints; verify the stroke passes checkpoints roughly in order. The counting half is a quantity-to-numeral match. Lenient checkpoint tolerance is simple.
designs.distinctiveness: Couples counting with generative numeral FORMATION by tracing — the child writes the answer numeral, linking cardinality to symbol production. Distinct from magic-trace (here the numeral is determined by counting, so the child must decide WHICH numeral before tracing) and from tap-the-number choices (they form it by hand). Lenient directional trace, not exact.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray ducks + faint outline numeral with arrows. CA5 art: pond, fuzzy ducklings, big dotted numerals with friendly arrow cues, cream + teal water.

designs.name: Bridge the Number Line
designs.mechanic: A number line is shown with a start number and a target. The child draws hop-arcs (jumps) above the line — each drawn arc snaps to span a whole-number jump — to get from start to target (e.g., from 3, draw two hops of +1 then... to reach 5, or one hop of +2). The sum of the drawn jumps must land exactly on the target, then a frog hops the arcs.
designs.fun_no_competition: Drawing springy arcs and watching a frog boing along them to land on the lily-pad target; arcs snap to whole numbers so they always look neat; overshoot just lets you redraw.
designs.character_world: A leapfrog crossing a pond by hopping numbered lily-pads along a number line.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — each drawn arc's horizontal span snaps to nearest integer jump; accumulate jumps and compare to target. The arc is cosmetic over a snapped integer delta — simple to evaluate.
designs.distinctiveness: Drawn jump-arcs encode addition/subtraction on a number line — the produced arcs ARE the equation. Distinct from the existing number-line manipulative (tap/slide a marker) because the child draws the decomposed hops, externalizing strategy, and from path-journey (no maze; the line + drawn arcs are the math).
designs.asset_idea: stub: horizontal line with ticks + plain arc. CA5 art: lily-pad number line, cheerful frog mid-leap, splash effects, teal pond, coral target pad.

designs.name: Trace the Letter, Hear the Sound
designs.mechanic: A prompt speaks a letter sound (/s/). The child must FORM that letter by tracing it along a faint, lenient stroke-order guide (decide which letter the sound makes, then write it). On a good trace the letter inks solid, its sound plays again, and a word starting with it pops up (s → sun).
designs.fun_no_competition: The letter filling in like wet ink as you trace and the sound/word reward; arrows guide stroke order; endlessly re-traceable, no marks-against. Audio note: whole-letter NAME and a whole WORD play (TTS-safe), the isolated /sound/ is delivered as a pre-recorded clip not TTS.
designs.character_world: A sound-spark snail that leaves a letter of ink wherever you trace, then names a picture word.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — letter stroke-path with ordered checkpoints + lenient tolerance; sound-to-letter is a mapping. Per the project's TTS finding, isolated phonemes use audio clips, not synthesis; letter names + whole words are TTS-safe.
designs.distinctiveness: Generative letter formation gated by phonics — the child chooses the letter from a SOUND then produces it by tracing, linking sound-symbol-formation. Distinct from magic-trace (the target letter isn't given, it's inferred from audio) and from tap-the-letter choices (they hand-form it). Forgiving stroke-order trace per L.K.1.a.
designs.asset_idea: stub: faint dotted letter + arrows + speaker icon. CA5 art: inky snail, glowing letter trail, reward picture (sun/cat), cream paper, teal ink.

designs.name: Cut Apart the Two Shapes
designs.mechanic: Two simple shapes are stuck together to make a composite (a square + triangle making a house outline, two rectangles making an L). The child draws a single cut line to separate the composite back into its two named component shapes; the cut snaps to the true seam and the pieces slide apart and label themselves.
designs.fun_no_competition: The clean slice that pops the house into a square and a triangle which then wear little name tags; the seam glows as a hint; off-cuts just bounce, redraw freely.
designs.character_world: A shape-tinkerer robot who builds things from two shapes and needs them taken apart to see how.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — composite has one true seam line; drawn stroke snaps to it within tolerance and triggers the pre-authored split. Single valid cut keeps evaluation a simple line-match.
designs.distinctiveness: Drawing a DE-composition cut along the join of a composite shape (compose/decompose geometry) — the cut line reveals the parts. Distinct from 01/05 (equal partitions of one shape) because here the line decomposes a composite into DIFFERENT named shapes, and from build-a-world (no assembling; the child separates).
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray composite outline + faint seam. CA5 art: blocky friendly robot, composite gadgets (house, rocket = triangle+rectangle), name-tag pieces, teal/coral.

designs.name: Color by Number-Word
designs.mechanic: A line-art picture is split into regions, each labeled with a number-word or a tiny sum ('three', 'two+one'). A palette maps numbers to colors. The child swipe-paints each region; the region accepts paint only if the chosen color matches its number-word/sum value, revealing the picture when all regions are correctly colored.
designs.fun_no_competition: The classic color-by-number calm — swiping color into outlined regions and the scene coming alive; a wrong color simply doesn't take (no harsh buzz), so it's pure, low-stakes coloring.
designs.character_world: A paint-pot parrot whose colorful jungle picture appears as you solve each region.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — SVG regions with a target-number attribute; selected palette color must match the region's solved value before fill applies. Region-snapped painting, simple gate.
designs.distinctiveness: Paint-to-reveal where the act of coloring is gated by reading number-words / solving small sums — generative shading that encodes a number↔color answer. Distinct from 08 (shade a fraction quantity) and reveal-grid (here the WHOLE picture is colored region-by-region and the gate is number-word literacy + addition).
designs.asset_idea: stub: outline picture with numbered regions + color palette. CA5 art: jungle scene (parrot, leaves, fruit), labeled regions, glossy paint pots, cream + tropical teal/coral.

designs.name: Ruler Lab
designs.mechanic: The child drags a ruler so its zero-end lines up with the start of an object, then taps the number on the ruler where the object ends to read its length. Tools snap-aligned but the child decides the reading.
designs.fun_no_competition: the satisfying click as the ruler snaps to zero and the glowing number where the object's tip lands — 'so THAT's how long it is!'
designs.character_world: a tiny inventor's workbench where curious critters bring odd objects (a pencil, a worm, a leaf) to be measured
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — draggable ruler sprite over a backdrop, scale ticks as DOM, tap-to-read
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid (tap to uncover), but here the CORE is physically positioning a measuring tool and reading a scale, not uncovering a hidden cell. Separation: the answer lives on a continuous scale the child reads, not a discrete grid cell.
designs.asset_idea: stub: gray ruler bar + numbered ticks + 6 object silhouettes; CA5: wooden ruler with brass ends, hand-drawn objects with measurable tips

designs.name: Unit-Train Lay-Down
designs.mechanic: The child drags identical unit-blocks (paper clips, cubes) end-to-end along an object until the object is fully covered, then counts the units laid to report the length. The experiment is figuring out how many units fit with no gaps or overlaps.
designs.fun_no_competition: the snap of each clip butting against the last, and the count climbing — 'it's six paper clips long!'
designs.character_world: a busy little ant crew laying a road of blocks across the garden
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — drag clones of a unit sprite with end-snap to the previous unit
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is build-a-world (place objects freely), but here placement is constrained to a measuring purpose — units MUST abut with no gaps. Separation from Ruler Lab: no pre-marked scale; the child constructs the unit count by iterating identical objects.
designs.asset_idea: stub: colored squares + object outline; CA5: chunky paper clips / wooden cubes with a friendly ant foreman

designs.name: Estimate-Then-Reveal Jar
designs.mechanic: A jar of objects is shown; the child first taps an estimate on a number-line slider (no counting allowed yet), THEN taps 'reveal' to count the items one-by-one as they hop out, comparing guess to actual. The skill is committing a reasoned guess before verifying.
designs.fun_no_competition: the gleeful 'how close was I?' reveal as candies hop out and the guess-marker and count-marker meet on the line
designs.character_world: a wondering owl who loves guessing jars at a sweet shop
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — slider DOM + sequential reveal animation of sprite instances
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is pop-the-right-ones, but nothing is 'wrong' here — the core is the predict-then-check loop: a committed estimate followed by a verified count. Separation: estimate-first sequencing is the mechanic, not selection.
designs.asset_idea: stub: glass jar + dots + horizontal slider; CA5: candy jar, hopping jellybeans, owl with a monocle

designs.name: Balance Discoverer
designs.mechanic: Two pans of a balance scale; the child loads an object onto each pan and watches the beam tip, discovering which is heavier by which side sinks. They can swap and re-test combinations until they can answer 'heavier / lighter'.
designs.fun_no_competition: the slow tilt of the beam and the 'clunk' — the apple wins! — pure cause-and-effect delight with no wrong move
designs.character_world: a fruit-bat shopkeeper weighing produce on an old market scale
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — CSS rotation of the beam keyed to a per-object weight value; drag objects to pans
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is sort-home (place items by category), but here placement is a TEST whose physical result (tipping) reveals the answer — the child experiments to discover weight order, not sort by a known label. Separation: the apparatus produces the verdict, not the child's prior knowledge.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two pans + pivot beam + weighted objects; CA5: brass market scale, ripe fruit, bat in an apron

designs.name: Pour-to-the-Line
designs.mechanic: The child tilts/taps a pitcher to pour liquid into a graduated container, stopping at a target fill-line shown on the side. They tune the pour to hit the marked level, reading the scale to know when to stop. Tighten so the child reads the graduated target and stops at the numbered fill-line (report/match the measured amount), making it instantiate 2.MD.A.1 measurement rather than a free pour; drop the 3.NF.A.1 line.
designs.fun_no_competition: the rising liquid and the 'just right!' chime when it reaches the line — gentle no-spill tinkering
designs.character_world: a friendly frog mixing pond-juice in a measuring cup
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fill-bar height driven by hold duration, target line as DOM marker
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is grow-tend (nurture over time), but the core here is calibrating a continuous quantity to a target reading on a measuring vessel — capacity, not growth. Separation: a measurable target line and a controllable pour, a tune-to-target loop.
designs.asset_idea: stub: beaker + fill rectangle + target line; CA5: measuring cup with painted gradations, dripping pitcher, frog barista

designs.name: Which Holds More?
designs.mechanic: Two differently-shaped containers; the child fills one, pours its contents into the other, and discovers whether it overflows, exactly fills, or leaves room — testing capacity directly rather than judging by appearance (tall-skinny vs short-wide). Require the child to PREDICT which holds more before the transfer and confirm by the result, so it instantiates K.MD.A.2 attribute-comparison reasoning rather than just observing a pour.
designs.fun_no_competition: the surprise — 'the skinny tall one held MORE?!' — overturning the look-bigger trap with a fun pour
designs.character_world: a tea-party hedgehog testing which cup holds the most cocoa
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fixed per-container capacity values; animate transfer and overflow
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is Pour-to-the-Line, but there the goal is hitting a line; here the goal is a COMPARISON discovered by transfer — does it overflow or not? Separation: the experiment is conservation-of-volume across shapes, surprising the eye.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two container outlines + liquid fill; CA5: mismatched whimsical teacups, steam, cozy hedgehog

designs.name: Tune-the-Dial Number
designs.mechanic: A dial/knob controls a big readout; the child rotates the dial until the displayed number matches a target shown by a character ('I want 7!'). Turning past or under is fine — they tune toward the value and watch it count up/down.
designs.fun_no_competition: the click-click of the dial and the readout flipping like an odometer until it locks green at the target
designs.character_world: a robot DJ who requests numbers on a glowing console
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — rotary drag → angle → integer mapping, flip-clock readout in DOM
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is magic-machine (input→transformed output), but no transformation happens — the dial IS the value and the child calibrates a continuous control to a target. Separation: tune-a-setting-to-a-target, not feed-and-transform.
designs.asset_idea: stub: knob + 7-seg display + target chip; CA5: retro radio dial, neon readout, boogie robot

designs.name: Combo Mixer Test
designs.mechanic: The child mixes two color/ingredient inputs and observes the result, testing combinations to discover which pairs make the target (blue+yellow→green). Free no-fail experimentation until they find the combo the character wants, with a record strip of what they've tried. Bind the win to reading/interpreting the tried-record data (which combination the chart shows works), so it instantiates K.MD.B.3 classify-and-interpret rather than free play; otherwise consider drop.
designs.fun_no_competition: the pop and swirl when two things mix — 'whoa, that made orange!' — endless safe what-if tinkering
designs.character_world: a paint-splattered octopus chemist in a bubbling lab
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — fixed combination lookup table, swatch reveal, tried-list as DOM chips
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is magic-machine (single input transformed), but here the child TESTS multiple combinations and the discovery is which combination produces an effect — a hypothesis-testing sandbox, plus an emergent data record. Separation: combinatorial test loop, not a fixed transform.
designs.asset_idea: stub: two input slots + result swatch + tried row; CA5: beakers, color splashes, goggled octopus

designs.name: Tally Tester Spinner
designs.mechanic: The child spins/taps a spinner many times and records each result into a tally chart, discovering through repeated trials which outcome comes up most. The experiment generates data the child reads off the chart.
designs.fun_no_competition: the random spin and the tally marks stacking up — 'star is winning the chart!' — discovery without a clock
designs.character_world: a carnival raccoon running a friendly prize wheel
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — randomized spinner, accumulate counts into a DOM bar/tally chart
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is sticker-album (collect into slots), but here the slot-filling is DATA collection from repeated trials and the payoff is reading 'which has the most' off the chart — represent-and-interpret data, not collection-completion. Separation: trial→record→interpret, an experiment producing a dataset.
designs.asset_idea: stub: spinner wheel + tally rows; CA5: carnival wheel with icons, chalkboard tally, raccoon barker

designs.name: Read-the-Diagram Detective (ELA)
designs.mechanic: An informational diagram (a labeled bug, a plant, a machine) is shown; a question asks 'find the part that does X' and the child taps the labeled part, using the diagram's labels and the caption to discover the answer. They test taps and read to confirm.
designs.fun_no_competition: the 'aha, the wings are for flying!' as the right label lights up — feels like real science detective work
designs.character_world: a magnifying-glass-toting ladybug naturalist labeling specimens
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — labeled hotspots over a diagram image, caption text in DOM
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is i-spy-scene (find an item visually), but here the find is driven by READING informational labels/captions to identify a part by its function — a use-text-features comprehension skill, not visual search. Separation: text-feature reading is the tool, the diagram is the data.
designs.asset_idea: stub: diagram image + label callouts + caption box; CA5: storybook nature diagram, leader lines, ladybug detective

designs.name: Thermometer Reader
designs.mechanic: A thermometer rises; the child reads the marked scale and taps the matching temperature (or drags a marker to where the mercury tops out). Variant: set the dial so the bath/oven reaches the 'just right' zone.
designs.fun_no_competition: the mercury climbing and a 'just right' band glowing — porridge-not-too-hot satisfaction
designs.character_world: a bear cub checking the temperature of three bowls of soup
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — vertical fill bar with tick scale, tap-to-read or drag marker
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is Ruler Lab (read a linear scale), but a thermometer is a vertical scale tied to a sensed state (warm/cold) and supports a set-to-target sub-mode. Separation: vertical scale + thermal context, distinct affordance and number-line tie.
designs.asset_idea: stub: vertical thermometer + ticks + marker; CA5: round-bulb thermometer, steamy soup bowls, sleepy bear

designs.name: Flashlight Phonics Cave
designs.mechanic: A dark cave wall hides many picture-objects in shadow. The child is told a target sound (e.g. /b/) and drags a flashlight beam across the wall; the beam softly illuminates whatever it passes over, but only objects whose NAME BEGINS with the target sound 'wake up' (glow, wiggle, smile) when lit. The child taps the glowing ones to collect them into a jar.
designs.fun_no_competition: Suspenseful sweep-and-discover in the dark; the delight of an object 'waking up' and glowing when your beam finds it; filling a glowing jar of collected sound-friends.
designs.character_world: A friendly cave-bat guide named Echo who lives in the Sound Cave and cheers when you wake a sleeping object.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — beam = a radial-gradient mask div following pointer; objects are absolutely-positioned sprites with opacity tied to beam proximity (CSS + a tiny pointermove handler), glow = CSS class toggled when name-onset matches.
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is i-spy-scene (find named items in a scene) and pop-the-right-ones. Separation: the items are HIDDEN in darkness and only the moving beam reveals them — discovery is spatial+continuous (sweep to expose) rather than a static scan, and the phonetic match is the gate for the reveal-glow itself, not just for scoring. The flashlight-as-reveal-tool is the core, not the tap.
designs.asset_idea: Stub: gray cave-wall bg + 8-10 grayscale object silhouettes + a cone-of-light PNG + glow halo. CA5 art: painted rock cave with cracks, Echo the bat, warm flashlight cone, per-object 'awake' (smiling) and 'asleep' (dim) frames.

designs.name: X-Ray Number Bones
designs.mechanic: A vet's x-ray table holds a stuffed animal; the child slides an x-ray scanner panel over it to reveal a hidden cluster of dots/bones inside. They must look at the revealed quantity and tap the numeral (or ten-frame) that matches how many they see — the dots stay revealed only while the scanner hovers, so they subitize/count under the lens.
designs.fun_no_competition: The novelty of x-ray vision; the gentle reveal of glowing bones inside a cuddly creature; satisfying 'ding' as the right number lights up and the animal gets a sticker bandage.
designs.character_world: Dr. Pip, a kindly toy-vet whose patients are plush animals that need a count of their tummy-dots.
designs.web_shell_feasibility: feasible — scanner is a draggable div with a clip/mask revealing a second 'inner' image layer; numeral choices are tappable tiles. No game loop; pure DOM masking.
designs.distinctiveness: Closest neighbor is reveal-grid (uncover a hidden picture).
